title: Changes nobody can find
summary: Use Git history to restore a file to a known-good commit.

scenario.briefing: A commit replaced the storefront status with broken text. The previous version is in history. Find the good commit and restore only the affected file without discarding other work.

objectives.description: Restore the file to its earlier content.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Run git log --oneline to see the commits.
The earlier commit contains the working version of src/store.js.
Check out that file from the earlier commit instead of resetting the whole repository.
Run git log --oneline, then git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/store.js, then git status.

misconceptions.description: Resetting the whole repository to fix one file.
misconceptions.feedback: A hard reset discards unrelated work. Restore only the affected file unless the evidence justifies a broader change.

misconceptions.description: Believing version control only stores the latest version.
misconceptions.feedback: Git commits form history. Earlier versions can be inspected and restored.

sections.title: Commits are snapshots with history
sections.body: A Git commit records a version of the project and points to its parent. The log shows the chain. Branches are movable names for commits, and HEAD is where the working tree currently sits.

sections.title: Restore deliberately
sections.body: Checking out one file from a commit changes that file without moving the branch. A hard reset moves the branch and can discard work. The right operation depends on how much state should change, not on which command sounds strongest.

vocabulary.definition: A recorded project snapshot with an identity and message.
The files currently present in the project folder.

steps.title: Restore the known-good file
steps.prompt: Use the terminal. Inspect history, restore src/store.js from the previous commit, and check status.
steps.explanation: The first commit contains the working status. Checking out that file version restores the known-good content without resetting the branch.

steps.title: What does checkout do?
steps.prompt: You run git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/store.js. What changes?

options.label: Only src/store.js is restored from the parent commit.
The entire project is reset to the parent commit.
The file is fetched from a remote server.

quiz.explanation: The -- path form checks out that file from the specified commit and leaves the branch and other files alone.

hints: The command names a file after the double dash.

steps.title: History and recovery

statements.label: A commit records a version of the project.
A single file can be restored without discarding unrelated changes.
A hard reset is always the safest repair.
Commits refer to parent commits, forming history.

steps.explanation: History makes earlier versions recoverable. The narrowest correct operation preserves unrelated work.

accessibility.summary: The Git terminal is a labeled text input with an output log. Suggested commands are visible as text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Type a command and press Enter. The output log can be scrolled with arrow keys.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The prompt announces the repository and branch. Command output is read in order, and checks report pass or fail.
